results.title: Foundation Consumer Healthcare Undergoes Major Leadership Changes to Focus on Women's Health Market - Third News
highlights:
In a bold move to reinforce its position in the burgeoning women's health sector, Foundation Consumer Healthcare (FCH) has announced significant changes in its senior leadership. Rupa Bahri, formerly of Haleon, has been appointed as the new CEO of the company, a strategic transition aimed at enhancing FCH's focus on women's health products. This change comes soon after the company successfully streamlined its portfolio, which included a targeted divestiture of its over-the-counter wellness brands to Prestige Consumer Healthcare in June 2026. The new appointment marks not just a change at the top but signals FCH's commitment to evolving into a dedicated player in women’s health. Rupa Bahri expressed her excitement about this new journey, stating, "I am honored to join Foundation Consumer Healthcare at such a transformative time. The team has an iconic brand in Plan B, and we have an opportunity to create an exceptional platform. Women's health represents one of the most dynamic and crucial opportunities in health care today." Under Bahri’s leadership, FCH aims to build on the strengths of its flagship brand, Plan B One-Step®, which is the top OB/GYN-recommended emergency contraception in the United States. The company intends to propel its product offerings in this vital area, enhancing education and access for women nationwide. Greg Bradley, the co-founder of FCH and its CEO since inception in 2014, will transition to the role of chairman of the board. Reflecting on his leadership journey, Bradley noted, "It has been a privilege to lead Foundation Consumer Healthcare over the past 12 years, a period during which we achieved phenomenal growth. With our focus now fully anchored on women's health, Rupa is exceptionally qualified to steer the company into this compelling next era." Rupa Bahri comes to FCH with more than two decades of experience in global healthcare. Her previous role as the Canadian president of Haleon saw her delivering remarkable growth in terms of market share and profitability. Additionally, her experience with U.S. portfolio turnarounds at Novartis Consumer and GSK Consumer Healthcare has prepared her to navigate the complexities of FCH’s future endeavors. As part of its strategic restructuring, FCH will not only concentrate on enhancing its existing women's health product line but also explore new ways to innovate and respond to consumer needs in this critical area. This shift aligns with broader trends in the healthcare market, which recognize women’s health as an often underserved but incredibly vital segment of patient care. Moreover, FCH’s commitment to women's health is underscored by its efforts to increase education and access to products like Plan B. The company believes that through innovative marketing strategies, it can better serve the needs of women across the country, ultimately contributing to a healthier society. The leadership transition comes at a time when women’s health is gaining increasing attention, and FCH aims to play a pivotal role in shaping future discussions and advancements in this area. The company’s clear alignment with this focus, alongside Bahri’s extensive background in driving strategic growth, positions it well for future successes. As FCH moves forward, the eyes of the industry will be on Rupa Bahri and her team. With a clear strategy and dedicated leadership, FCH is poised to establish itself as a leader in the women's health sector, ensuring that it not only meets the needs of consumers today but also paves the way for innovations that could benefit future generations. Through this strategic repositioning, Foundation Consumer Healthcare looks to cultivate a legacy marked by empowerment, education, and exceptional health outcomes for women everywhere.
